title: Liking electric bass: reliability, ease and effects
summary: He finds the electric bass clean and easy, never failed him, and still loves string bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, does it change your plan?

I really like it. I really like it, because I find it clean, the notes are real clean, and I just forgot about the electrical end of it having to phase out, because I've got a spare. I can always jump to a spare, you know, even though I keep the spare at home, you know what I mean? But I could have a spare on the job in a half hour's time.
Well, you never had a problem.
It's never failed me yet. Yeah. It's never failed me yet.
I wish I could say the same for tape recording.

That used to be my main worry about bass guitar. Well, if you have a power failure, or you blow a fuse, well, all bass guitar players carry spare fuses. Stick a spare fuse. A spare fuse would be in your amplifier, not in your bass. And I haven't even blown a fuse since I'm playing guitar, bass, and it's about seven years. It's never let me down yet. So I'm real happy with it now. I enjoy playing it. And it's much easier to get around. It's like carrying a violin now instead of a great big bass violin.
Well, can you get around on it physically and play more notes or less notes?
Well, like I say, being an old guitar player, it came easier to me.
Yeah, so you could...
I would say it's much easier than string bass. It is. To me, it's easier than string bass.
Yeah.
String bass is hard.
Yeah. Well, I noticed that it does change the line.

And I played string bass 37 years. And this has frets on it, and the string bass doesn't have frets. So, you know, and being an old guitar player for four years, it came to me quicker than I anticipated. So I really like it. I can truthfully say I really like guitar, bass. I know a lot of the old timers like the string bass now. And I don't dislike string bass. I still love string bass, and I love to hear good bass players. I'm not putting down string bass at all because I played it for 37 years, and I really like it. But in my particular case, I'm very happy with the guitar bass because there's quite a few of them around the country. Even the Doc Severson band playing guitar bass now. You find more and more of them every year. I really like it.
Do you ever use the fuzz tone and those effects? Anything like that?
How do you mean the fuzz tone?
Well, they have something switch. It's a pedal.
Oh, no. You're talking about electric guitars now.
No.
No.
I've seen...
Not for bass.
Joey's French. Get some very strange sounds out of them.
Oh, all he's just doing is running his hand up and down.
